And during your cross-examination, I believe that those issues are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not quite following you, Your Honour. Legal issues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think during cross-examination there are some legal issues that are mentioned on which Mr. Deronjic is entitled to have his Defence counsel. But as to the factual issues as to whether he met with Mr. Karadzic or not, whether on that day and as for the contents of the conversation, I don't think the counsel should be consulted on those issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you don't trust the counsel --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I didn't say that, Your Honour. I don't -- I've been practicing for 20 years. I know and I've represented thousands of clients and they have an overwhelming urge to ask questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that if we furnish the transcript of today's proceedings to Mr. Deronjic's counsel, and I think our warnings are there in the transcript. They could read it, and Mr. Deronjic is entitled to consult with his counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on your -- I wasn't aware that there were legal issues, and I -- perhaps because it's late in the day. I accept that. And I think Mr. Deronjic has been told now on the record that they are not to be talking about the issues. So I'm satisfied with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think for the witness -- I mean, it's pretty clear to me that you just said he could talk with his client about the legal issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's what I said. I agreed to that. I just agreed to that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You just said he couldn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He could. I'm getting tired, maybe I'm not annunciating as well. Maybe I'm getting tired. He could talk about the legal issues, as you indicated, but not about the specific facts. I don't have a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Witness, you hear the rulings of this Bench and you are entitled to talk to your counsel on the legal issues, but not on the factual issues. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me just one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As part of my obligations that are already specified and established before this Tribunal, a hearing is pending regarding the acts I pled guilty to. That's scheduled for the 27th, on Tuesday, before another Trial Chamber. Also clear are my obligations regarding testifying. These are very serious obligations, to which I have already agreed. The previous arrangement was that I testify for only two days, and I have nothing against it going on longer. But in view of the fact that I have scheduled meetings with my counsel and the administration of the Detention Unit agreed to allow us to hold consultations on Friday through Sunday in order to prepare properly, I thought it fitting to have some opportunity to rest tomorrow. If it is absolutely necessary for me to come here again tomorrow, I agree. But I am under a certain strain and I do need some rest. I am not quite clear now whether this restriction can be viewed in that light. I don't think that's what it means. I need to meet with my counsel in order to prepare for the hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I apologise for the delay. Originally we arranged the hearings for two days, only for two days, that is the fact. But there are a lot of issues, especially during the cross-examination as you understand it. So I would like to ask for your cooperation that we continue to sit tomorrow. And tomorrow afternoon from 3.00 to 4.30 we will add another session. And the -- so that you could have time on Friday to talk with your Defence counsel on another hearing which is scheduled next Tuesday. I apologise for this delay, but sometimes it happens. I hope you could understand that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will of course accept this. I will be here again tomorrow, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation on this aspect. And tomorrow morning we'll resume at 9.00 in the same courtroom, and we'll continue to sit in Courtroom I at 3.00 until 4.30. The hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 1.55 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of January, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
